arxiv-2008-02070.title: Content based singing voice source separation via strong conditioning using aligned phonemes
arxiv-2008-02070.description: Abstract Informed source separation has recently gained renewed interest with the introduction of neural networks and the availability of large multitrack datasets containing both the mixture and the separated sources. These approaches use prior information about the target source to improve separation.

arxiv-2108-10744.title: Interpretable deep-learning models to help achieve the Sustainable Development Goals
arxiv-2108-10744.creator: Ricardo Vinuesa, Beril Sirmacek
arxiv-2108-10744.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ricardo Vinuesa, Beril Sirmacek. We discuss our insights into interpretable artificial-intelligence (AI) models, and how they are essential in the context of developing ethical AI systems, as well as data-driven solutions compliant with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). We highlight the potential of extracting truly-interpretable models from deep-learning methods, for instance via symbolic models obtained through inductive biases, to ensure a sustainable development of AI.

arxiv-2112-09022.title: Correct and accurate polymorphic energy ordering of transition-metal monoxides obtained from semilocal and onsite-hybrid exchange-correlation approximations
arxiv-2112-09022.creator: Arghya Ghosh, Subrata Jana, Manish K Niranjan, Fabien Tran, David Wimberger, Peter Blaha, Lucian A. Constantin, Prasanjit Samal
arxiv-2112-09022.description: Abstract The relative energetic stability of the structural phases of common antiferromagnetic transition-metal oxides (MnO, FeO, CoO, and NiO) within the semilocal and hybrid density functionals are fraught with difficulties. In particular, MnO is known to be the most difficult case for almost all common semilocal and hybrid density approximations.

arxiv-2207-03223.title: Realistic 3D hydrodynamics simulations find significant turbulent entrainment in massive stars 2022 Realistic 3D hydrodynamics simulations find significant turbulent entrainment in massive stars – References
arxiv-2207-03223.creator: F. Rizzuti, R. Hirschi, C. Georgy, W. D. Arnett, C. Meakin, A. StJ. Murphy
arxiv-2207-03223.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by F. Rizzuti, R. Hirschi, C. Georgy, W. D. Arnett, C. Meakin, A. StJ. Murphy. Our understanding of stellar structure and evolution coming from one-dimensional (1D) stellar models is limited by uncertainties related to multi-dimensional processes taking place in stellar interiors. 1D models, however, can now be tested and improved with the help of detailed three-dimensional (3D) hydrodynamics models, which can reproduce complex multi-dimensional processes over short timescales, thanks to the recent advances in computing resources.

arxiv-2308-03074.title: Non-Fermi Liquid Behavior of the t t - J J Model in the Strange Metal Phase: U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) Gauge Theory Consistent with Local Constraints
arxiv-2308-03074.creator: Long Liang, Yue Yu, Xi Luo
arxiv-2308-03074.description: Abstract In the slave particle representation with U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) gauge symmetry, local constraints on physical states characterized by various mean field solutions belong to Dirac’s second-class ones. Although constrained systems are extensively investigated, realistic methods to solve the gauge theory problem with second-class constraints are yet to be developed.

arxiv-2411-11652.title: On the Incorporation of Stability Constraints into Sequential Operational Scheduling
arxiv-2411-11652.creator: Wangkun Xu, Zhongda Chu, Florin Capitanescu, Fei Teng
arxiv-2411-11652.description: Abstract With the increasing penetration of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs), power system stability constraints must be incorporated into the operational framework, transforming it into stability-constrained optimization. Currently, there exist parallel research efforts on developing the stability constraints within DC power flow-based unit commitment (UC) and AC Optimal Power Flow (OPF).

arxiv-2502-01515.title: (Anti-)Altermagnetism from Orbital Ordering in the Ruddlesden-Popper Chromates Sr n+1 Cr n O 3n+1
arxiv-2502-01515.creator: Quintin N. Meier, Alberto Carta, Claude Ederer, Andrés Cano
arxiv-2502-01515.description: Abstract Altermagnets form a subclass of collinear antiferromagnets with spin-split electronic states. Here, we introduce the Ruddlesden-Popper chromates Sr n+1 Cr n O 3n+1 (including the perovskite SrCrO 3 ) as candidates for antiferromagnetic materials in which altermagnetism emerges from spontaneous orbital ordering, rather than crystal symmetry.

arxiv-2506-07452.title: When Style Breaks Safety: Defending Language Models Against Superficial Style Alignment
arxiv-2506-07452.creator: Yuxin Xiao, Sana Tonekaboni, Walter Gerych, Vinith Suriyakumar, Marzyeh Ghassemi
arxiv-2506-07452.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuxin Xiao, Sana Tonekaboni, Walter Gerych, Vinith Suriyakumar, Marzyeh Ghassemi. Large language models (LLMs) can be prompted with specific styles (e.g., formatting responses as lists), including in jailbreak queries. Although these style patterns are semantically unrelated to the malicious intents behind jailbreak queries, their safety impact remains unclear. In this work, we seek to understand whether style patterns compromise LLM safety, how superficial style alignment increases model vulnerability, and how best to mitigate these risks during alignment.

pmc-11687261.title: GPs’ reflections on prescribing addictive hypnotics to older people: a qualitative study
pmc-11687261.creator: Holgeir Skjeie, Mette Brekke, Trygve Skonnord
pmc-11687261.description: BackgroundThe European guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of insomnia recommends, for all age groups, only restrictive, short-term, and periodic use of potentially addictive hypnotics. As in other European countries, in Norway, actual practice involving older patients differs substantially from this recommendation, as shown by the persistent high frequency of regular prescriptions of addictive hypnotics.

pmc-12566990.title: Early Detection and Identification of Methylobacterium radiotolerans Bacteremia in an Early T-Cell Precursor Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Patient: A Rare Infection and Literature Review
pmc-12566990.creator: Jiayu Xiao, Lingli Liu, Xuzhen Qin, Yingchun Xu, Longzhu Cui
pmc-12566990.description: (1) Background: Methylobacterium radiotolerans (M. radiotolerans) is a fastidious, aerobic, Gram-negative bacillus primarily found in environmental sources such as soil and sewage, with rare clinical isolation. Its identification remains challenging due to poor growth with conventional culture methods. (2) Case presentation: A 42-year-old male patient with early T-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ETP-ALL) presented with M. radiotolerans bacteremia during hospitalization.
